name: HippoRAG

paper.title: HippoRAG: Neurobiologically Inspired Long-Term Memory for Large Language Models

construction.unit: passage (kept verbatim) plus open-IE triples extracted from it
construction.kept_as: verbatim passages; LLM-extracted (noun phrase, relation, noun phrase) triples as the index
construction.processing: 1-shot NER on each passage, then 1-shot OpenIE given those entities; phrases lower-cased and stripped of punctuation

organization.structure: schemaless KG: phrase nodes, triple edges and synonymy edges, plus node-to-passage links
organization.index: retrieval-encoder vectors of node phrases (ColBERTv2 or Contriever); synonymy edges between phrases with similarity ≥ 0.8

management.operations: new passages add nodes and edges; nothing is summarised or rewritten

retrieval.query: LLM extracts named entities from the question (1-shot)
retrieval.candidates: each query entity linked to its single most similar KG node; Personalized PageRank from these seeds, weighted by node specificity (1/#passages)
retrieval.selection: passages ranked by the PPR probability of the phrases in their triples; top-k
retrieval.budget: top-5 passages to the reader; top-10 per step inside IRCoT

use.reasoning: 1-shot CoT reader; optionally inside IRCoT (2-4 retrieve-reason steps)

classify.note: Dense vectors only link query entities to one node each; the ranking itself comes from PageRank over the graph, then a plain top-k of passages.

stages.ingestion: A fixed corpus of passages (all candidate passages of 1,000 dev questions per dataset) is indexed offline in one batch.
stages.construction: An LLM first lists the named entities of each passage, then extracts open-IE triples that should contain those entities; the triples' subject and object phrases become KG nodes.
stages.organization: Nodes are joined by triple edges (weighted by how often the pair co-occurs in triples) and by synonymy edges between phrases whose encoder similarity is at least 0.8; each node keeps links to the passages it came from.
stages.update: The paper argues new passages can be added by adding nodes and edges, without re-summarising; the experiments index a fixed corpus once.
stages.retrieval: Query entities from a 1-shot LLM NER are linked to their closest nodes, seeded with weight 1/#passages, and Personalized PageRank (damping 0.5) spreads probability over the KG; passages are scored by the probability of their phrases.
stages.answer: The top-5 passages go to a 1-shot CoT reader (GPT-3.5-turbo-1106); in IRCoT mode each reasoning step's thought is used as the next query.

summary: Retrieval memory modelled on hippocampal indexing: an LLM turns every passage into an open knowledge graph, and a question's entities seed Personalized PageRank over that graph so passages linked through shared entities are found in one step.

The id 'hipporag' was already an extra_systems baseline; this file annotates the same system (HippoRAG 2 is the separate id hipporag-v2).
DESIGN: §2.2-2.3 (indexing, retrieval, node specificity), §3.4 and App. H (settings), App. I (prompts). Code: the repo's main branch is HippoRAG 2; the v1 code is the 'legacy' branch, tagged v1.0.0. management.timing is 'offline' because indexing is a batch step and nothing changes at question time.

headline: The graph is only an index: the reader gets the top-5 original passages, never triples, nodes or PPR scores.
Each query entity is linked to exactly one node; everything else reached comes from PageRank spreading over triple and synonymy edges.
Relation labels are extracted but not used in scoring: graph edges carry only co-occurrence counts or similarity.

fields.what: ColBERTv2 or Contriever encoding, used to link query entities and to add synonymy edges

fields.name: node specificity
fields.what: 1 / number of passages the phrase occurs in; weights seed nodes

1-shot prompt given the passage and its entity list returns triples that should contain at least one, preferably two, of those entities; pronouns resolved
subject and object phrases become nodes; each triple adds 1 to the weight of the edge between them; document-triple and triple-phrase matrices kept
for each phrase with more than 2 letters or digits, add edges to its nearest phrases (encoder kNN) while similarity ≥ 0.8, up to about 100

read.how: sum node probabilities over each triple's two phrases, then over the passage's triples; min-max normalise; sort

answer_context.format: system instruction + 1 CoT demonstration, then each of the 5 passages as 'Wikipedia Title: {title}\n{text}', then 'Question: …\nThought: '
answer_context.note: In IRCoT mode the reader is replaced by IRCoT's interleaved reasoning, with HippoRAG as its retriever (top 10 per step).
answer_context.src: paper App. H; code qa_reader.py L38-L70, L85-L104

compression.what: reader context vs the retrieval corpus
compression.basis: Not reported as tokens. The reader reads 5 of 11,656 / 6,119 / 9,221 passages (Table 1, App. H); passage lengths are not given.

paper_vs_code.paper: PPR node probabilities times a node x passage count matrix
paper_vs_code.code: probabilities summed through triples (each phrase counted once per triple it is in), then min-max normalised

paper_vs_code.paper: all phrase pairs with similarity above τ
paper_vs_code.code: only among each phrase's nearest ~100 neighbours, skipping phrases with 2 or fewer letters/digits; edge weight = similarity
default 0.1 in the class and CLI; the main-experiment script passes 0.5

open_questions: HotpotQA R@5 stays below ColBERTv2 (77.7 vs 79.3); the paper attributes this to weaker multi-hop requirements and the concept-context trade-off (App. B, F.2).
Scalability beyond ~10k-passage corpora is untested, by the authors' own statement.

discussion.takeaway: Indexing a corpus as an LLM-built open knowledge graph and ranking passages with Personalized PageRank from the question's entities retrieves multi-hop evidence in a single step, beating dense retrievers on MuSiQue and 2WikiMultiHopQA and matching iterative IRCoT at far lower online cost.

claims.claim: Single-step retrieval beats standard and LLM-augmented retrievers on multi-hop QA.
claims.evidence: R@5 2Wiki 89.1 vs 68.2 (ColBERTv2), MuSiQue 51.9 vs 50.1 (best baseline); HotpotQA slightly lower (77.7 vs 79.3). Table 2, §4.

claims.claim: HippoRAG and iterative retrieval are complementary.
claims.evidence: IRCoT + HippoRAG R@5 57.6 / 93.9 / 83.0 vs IRCoT + ColBERTv2 53.7 / 74.4 / 82.0. Table 3.
F1 with a GPT-3.5 reader: 2Wiki 59.5 vs 43.3 (ColBERTv2); IRCoT + HippoRAG best on all three (33.3 / 62.7 / 59.2). Table 4.

claims.claim: PPR is what makes the graph useful.
claims.evidence: Query nodes only: average R@5 56.2 vs 72.9 with PPR. Table 5.

claims.claim: Single-step multi-hop: all supporting passages retrieved more often.
claims.evidence: AR@5 75.7 vs 37.1 on 2Wiki, 22.4 vs 16.1 on MuSiQue. Table 6.

claims.claim: Much cheaper and faster than iterative retrieval online.
claims.evidence: $0.1 and 3 min per 1,000 queries vs $1-3 and 20-40 min for IRCoT. Table 17, App. G.

limits: All components are used off the shelf; most errors come from NER and OpenIE (48% and 28% of 100 MuSiQue errors), which fine-tuning could reduce.
PPR errors remain; letting relations guide the graph walk is left for future work.
OpenIE quality drops on longer passages.
Scalability to much larger indexes is not yet shown.
reading: The reader only ever sees raw passages; the KG changes which passages are chosen, not what is read.
Relation labels are not used anywhere in scoring (edges carry counts or similarity), which matches the authors' note that relations do not yet guide the walk.
Query NER keeps only entities, so non-entity cues in the question are lost; this is the largest error class (48%, Table 11).
Main results use corpora built from the candidate passages of 1,000 dev questions each (6k-12k passages), much smaller than open-domain settings.
QA is reported only for the ColBERTv2 variant and against ColBERTv2 and IRCoT, not the LLM-augmented baselines (RAPTOR, Propositionizer).

abstract.text: HippoRAG is a retrieval framework modelled on the hippocampal indexing theory of long-term memory. Offline, an LLM turns every passage into open knowledge-graph triples, and a retrieval encoder adds edges between similar phrases, forming an index over the corpus. Online, the question's named entities are linked to graph nodes and Personalized PageRank spreads relevance from them, so passages connected through shared entities are found in one retrieval step. On multi-hop QA (MuSiQue, 2WikiMultiHopQA, HotpotQA) it beats standard retrievers by up to 20% and rivals iterative retrieval at a fraction of the cost and time.
